## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
#Step 1.3
#Now using R, plot the histogram of coverage across the genome. Overlay the histogram with a Poisson distribution with lambda = 3. Also overlay the distribution with a Normal distribution with a mean of 3 and a std. dev. of 1.73 (which is the square root of 3).
genomecov_df <- read.table("~/qb25-answers/week11/genome_coverage.txt")
normalest_df <- read.table("~/qb25-answers/week11/normal_estimates.txt")
poissonest_df <- read.table("~/qb25-answers/week11/poisson_estimates.txt")


coverage <- scan("genome_coverage.txt")

max_cov <- max(coverage)
values <- 0:max_cov

poisson_prob <- dpois(values, lambda = 3)

normal_prob <- dnorm(values, mean = 3, sd = sqrt(3))

distrib <- data.frame(
  coverage = rep(values, 2),
  density = c(poisson_prob, normal_prob),
  type = rep(c("Poisson", "Normal"), each = length(values))
)


ex1_3x_cov <- ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = coverage, y = ..density..),
                 bins = 50,
                 fill = "lightblue",
                 color = "black",
                 alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(x = coverage, y = density, color = type),
            data = distrib, size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Poisson" = "red", "Normal" = "darkgreen")) +
  labs(title = "Genome Coverage Distribution",
       x = "Coverage",
       y = "Density",
       color = "Distribution") 
ggsave(plot = ex1_3x_cov, filename = "ex1_3x_cov.png", path= "~/qb25-answers/week11")
?scan()
#HINT: For the poisson and normal distributions, you’ll need to find the probability of getting a certain coverage. For the poisson distribution, this is called the probability mass function (PMF) of the distribution. Feel free to code this yourself using the appropriate equation, or you can take a look at the python scipy.stats.poisson.pmf() function (more here) or the R dpois function (more here). Unlike the Poisson distribution, the normal distribution is continuous, and so we will instead want to use the probability density function (PDF). Note that for both of these, this will give you the probability of observing each coverage. What do we need to do to transform these probabilities into a frequency count comparable to those in our histogram?


#Upload this plot as ex1_3x_cov.png in your submission directory. All plots should be clearly labelled and easily interpretable (i.e. axis labels, legend describing the three things plotted, etc.).
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
#Step 1.5
#Now, repeat the analysis with 10x coverage:
poisson_prob_2 <- dpois(values, lambda =10)

normal_prob_2 <- dnorm(values, mean = 10, sd = 3.16)
#Simulate using the appropriate number of reads


distrib_2 <- data.frame(
  coverage = rep(values, 2),
  density = c(poisson_prob_2, normal_prob_2),
  type = rep(c("Poisson", "Normal"), each = length(values))
)
#In R, make a histogram. Overlay a Poisson distribution with lambda = 10. Overlay a Normal distribution with mean = 10 and std. dev. = 3.16. Upload this plot as ex1_10x_cov.png in your submission directory.

ex1_10x_cov <- ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = coverage, y = ..density..),
                 bins = 50,
                 fill = "lightblue",
                 color = "black",
                 alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(x = coverage, y = density, color = type),
            data = distrib_2, size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Poisson" = "red", "Normal" = "darkgreen")) +
  labs(title = "Genome Coverage Distribution",
       x = "Coverage",
       y = "Density",
       color = "Distribution") 
ggsave(plot = ex1_10x_cov, filename = "ex1_10x_cov.png", path= "~/qb25-answers/week11")
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
